bio_evolution.caption: Five forces change a population over generations: mutation supplies variants, selection sorts them, drift and gene flow shuffle frequencies, and speciation splits lineages.

bio_natural_selection.caption: Breeder's equation: the offspring mean moves by R = h²S, the heritable part of the selection differential. Raise S or h² and the gold curve shifts further from the parents.

bio_selection_modes.caption: Three fitness shapes: directional (green) favours one extreme, stabilising (gold) the middle, disruptive (pink) both ends. Slide the population mean and see which mode would raise or lower its fitness.

bio_sexual_selection.caption: A showy trait earns more matings (green, saturating) but costs survival (pink); fitness is their product (gold) and peaks at a compromise. Raise the cost and the optimum shrinks.

bio_evidence_for_evolution.caption: Amino-acid differences in cytochrome c (104 residues) from the human protein: the more recent the common ancestor, the fewer the differences.

bio_species_concepts.caption: Biological (interbreeding), morphological (looks), phylogenetic (one clade), ecological (niche) and genetic (DNA gap) concepts emphasise different evidence; they usually agree on well-studied groups and disagree on borderline ones.

bio_speciation_mechanisms.caption: Genetic differentiation between two populations falls as gene flow rises: Fst ≈ 1/(1 + 4Nm). With fewer than one migrant per generation, populations drift apart and can speciate.

bio_adaptive_radiation.caption: Darwin's finches radiated from one ancestor into species that specialise in different foods, each with a matching beak.

bio_phylogeny_cladistics.caption: A cladogram groups organisms by shared derived traits: each node is a common ancestor, and each clade includes all of its descendants.

bio_molecular_clock.caption: If mutations accumulate at a steady rate, sequence divergence is a clock: d = 2μt (both lineages change). Read off the time of the split from the observed divergence.

params.label: rate μ (% per Myr per lineage)

bio_geologic_time.caption: Earth is 4.54 Gyr old; the animal-rich Phanerozoic is only the last 12% of it. Bars show the length of each eon.

bio_mass_extinctions.caption: Estimated share of marine species lost in each of the five mass extinctions, at about 445, 372, 252, 201 and 66 Ma (approximate); the end-Permian was the worst.

bio_macroevolution_evodevo.caption: Small changes in regulatory genes such as Hox can reshape the whole body plan, because they set what each segment becomes.

bio_neutral_theory_drift.caption: For a neutral allele starting at frequency 0.5, random drift spreads the frequency out over time: the ±2 SD band widens faster in small populations. Slide N to see the difference.

bio_kin_selection_behavior_evo.caption: Hamilton's rule: a helping gene spreads when r·b > c. The curve is the minimum benefit b = c/r needed; closer relatives (higher r) need less.

bio_human_evolution.caption: Average cranial capacity of hominins (approximate): brains roughly tripled over about 3.5 million years.

bio_origin_of_life.caption: Key dates in billions of years ago: Earth forms, oceans, first life, photosynthesis, oxygen rise, eukaryotes, animals. Life is almost as old as the oceans; animals arrived late.

bio_rna_world_luca.caption: A likely route from chemistry to cells: self-copying RNA, then encapsulation, then DNA and proteins, ending in the last universal common ancestor.

bio_evolution_misconceptions.caption: Mutation is random but selection is not, and evolution has no goal: populations adapt to the conditions they actually face.

bio_experimental_evolution.caption: In Lenski's long-term E. coli experiment, fitness relative to the ancestor keeps rising for tens of thousands of generations, with diminishing returns. The curve is schematic.

bio_diversity.caption: Described species per group, in thousands (approximate): insects alone outnumber all plants, fungi and vertebrates together.

bio_fungi_basics.caption: A fungus lives as a network of hyphae (mycelium), absorbing food from outside; fruiting bodies are only the reproductive tip.

bio_fungal_ecology.caption: Fungi play several ecological roles: they recycle dead matter, partner with roots and algae, and can attack hosts.

bio_algae_green_origin.caption: Land plants arose from a group of freshwater green algae (charophytes), and later lineages added vascular tissue, seeds and flowers.

bio_bryophytes_seedless.caption: Plants alternate between a haploid gametophyte (n) and a diploid sporophyte (2n). In mosses the gametophyte dominates; in ferns the sporophyte does.

bio_seed_plants.caption: Seed plants split into naked-seed gymnosperms and flowering angiosperms, whose seeds develop inside a fruit.

bio_animal_features.caption: Animals branch by body symmetry, number of germ layers and how the mouth forms, from asymmetric sponges to bilateral deuterostomes.

bio_sponges_cnidarians.caption: A cnidarian polyp has radial symmetry: tentacles ring a single mouth that leads to a gut with one opening. Use the slider to extend the tentacles.

bio_lophotrochozoans.caption: Lophotrochozoans include flatworms, annelids (segmented worms) and mollusks, which share a trochophore-type larva or a lophophore.

bio_nematodes_arthropods.caption: Ecdysozoans molt their cuticle. Arthropods, the largest animal phylum, split into four main lineages.

bio_entomology_insects.caption: Described species per insect order, in thousands (approximate): beetles dominate, which is why Haldane quipped about the Creator's "inordinate fondness for beetles".

bio_echinoderms_chordates.caption: Echinoderms and chordates are both deuterostomes. Chordates include tunicates, lancelets and vertebrates, all sharing a notochord at some stage.

bio_fishes_amphibians.caption: Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes; amphibians are the first lineage to live on land, still tied to water to breed.

bio_reptiles_birds.caption: Birds are living dinosaurs: they nest within the archosaur branch alongside crocodilians, and share an amniotic egg with all reptiles and mammals.

bio_mammals_primates.caption: Mammals split into egg-laying monotremes, pouched marsupials and placentals; primates (monkeys, apes and humans) are one placental branch.

bio_zoology_taxonomy_methods.caption: Lincoln–Petersen mark–recapture: mark M animals, later catch C and find R already marked; then N ≈ M·C/R. Fewer recaptures means a bigger population.

bio_plants.caption: A plant is a system of organs that work together: roots take up water and minerals, leaves make sugar, and the vascular system links them while hormones coordinate growth.

bio_plant_body_tissues.caption: Every plant organ is built from three tissue systems that run through root, stem and leaf: dermal (skin), ground (fills and stores) and vascular (xylem and phloem), grown from meristems at the tips.

bio_leaf_structure_gas_exchange.caption: In a leaf cross-section, CO₂ enters and water vapour leaves through stomata. Open the stomata and gas flows; close them and water is saved but photosynthesis slows.

bio_water_transport.caption: Water potential falls with height: gravity costs about 0.01 MPa per metre, and friction in the xylem adds more when transpiration is strong. Raise the flow loss and the top of a tall tree nears cavitation risk.

bio_phloem_transport.caption: In pressure-flow, loading sugar at the source raises turgor and unloading at the sink lowers it, so sap streams down the pressure gradient. Raise the pressure difference to speed the flow.

bio_plant_nutrition_soil.caption: Typical mineral content of dry plant tissue (percent of dry mass): nitrogen and potassium are needed most, but all of these macronutrients are essential.

bio_photosynthetic_adaptations.caption: C4 plants concentrate CO₂ and so photosynthesise well at low CO₂, with no loss to photorespiration; C3 plants gain more as CO₂ rises. Slide the ambient CO₂ to compare.

bio_plant_hormones.caption: Auxin promotes stem elongation at concentrations that inhibit roots; roots respond at much lower doses. The curves are schematic. Move the slider to compare the effect at one concentration.

bio_plant_responses.caption: Short-day plants flower when nights are longer than a critical length; long-day plants when nights are shorter. It is night length, not day length, that the plant measures.

bio_plant_reproduction.caption: A flowering plant's life cycle: pollen reaches the stigma, grows a tube, and double fertilisation forms the embryo and its food store, all inside a seed.

bio_plant_development_flower.caption: The ABC model: A alone makes sepals, A+B petals, B+C stamens, C alone carpels. Switch off A function (apetala2 mutant) and C spreads outward, giving carpel–stamen–stamen–carpel.

bio_animal_phys.caption: Animals solve the same problems — getting food and oxygen, moving them around, removing waste, keeping conditions steady — with different organ systems.

bio_animal_form_scaling.caption: Kleiber's law: metabolic rate scales as body mass to the power ≈ 0.75, so big animals use less energy per kilogram. Change the exponent and compare with simple proportionality (slope 1).

bio_energy_budgets_nutrition.caption: Energy released per gram of food: fat packs more than twice the energy of carbohydrate or protein.

bio_comparative_digestion.caption: A ruminant digests grass in four stomach chambers; food returns to the mouth as cud so microbes in the rumen can ferment cellulose.

bio_comparative_circulation.caption: Mammals and birds have double circulation: the right heart pumps blood to the lungs, the left heart to the body, so tissues receive fully oxygenated blood at high pressure.

bio_comparative_respiration.caption: Fick's law: diffusion rate ∝ surface area × pressure difference ÷ thickness. Gills and lungs are thin and folded for exactly this reason. Increase the area or thin the barrier to raise gas flux.

bio_oxygen_transport_diving.caption: Myoglobin grabs oxygen at far lower PO₂ than haemoglobin, storing it in muscle for diving. Shift haemoglobin's P50 (higher in acid or heat, lower in e.g. llamas) and watch the curve move.

bio_osmoregulation.caption: Approximate osmolarity (mOsm/L): freshwater fish must pump out water and keep salt, while marine fish keep blood saltier than their body but far below seawater.

bio_excretion_nitrogen.caption: Animals excrete nitrogen as ammonia (cheap but toxic, needs lots of water), urea (less toxic) or uric acid (a paste that saves water).

bio_thermoregulation_animals.caption: An endotherm's metabolism rises in the cold and heat; an ectotherm's rate follows temperature with a Q10 effect. Move the slider to compare the two at one body or air temperature.

bio_locomotion_skeletons.caption: The forearm is a third-class lever: the biceps pulls close to the elbow, so it must pull much harder than the weight it holds. Move the attachment point to change the force needed.

bio_endocrine_comparative.caption: The hypothalamus–pituitary–thyroid axis is a negative-feedback loop: the final hormone (T4) switches off its own drivers, holding the level steady.

bio_reproduction_strategies.caption: Eggs or offspring per female per breeding event (log scale, approximate): some animals invest in one offspring, others broadcast millions.

bio_neuro.caption: Neuroscience spans levels from ion channels to behaviour: cells and signals at the bottom, circuits and brain regions above, and the senses and behaviour they produce.

bio_neuron_glia.caption: A neuron receives signals on dendrites, integrates them in the soma and sends a spike down the myelinated axon to its terminals. Watch the impulse travel; it jumps between gaps in the myelin.

bio_action_potential_channels.caption: An all-or-none spike: depolarise past the −55 mV threshold and voltage-gated Na⁺ channels trigger a full action potential; a smaller stimulus fades away. Increase the stimulus to cross threshold.

bio_synapse_neurotransmitters.caption: One EPSP is too small to fire the neuron, but two arriving close together add up (temporal summation) and cross threshold. Shrink the gap between inputs to see summation grow.

bio_synaptic_plasticity_memory.caption: After a brief high-frequency burst (t = 0), synaptic strength jumps (LTP). Early LTP fades in about an hour; with protein synthesis the late phase lasts. Slide the decay time to compare.

bio_sensory_transduction.caption: Stevens' power law: perceived intensity = k·Sᵃ. Brightness (a≈0.33) compresses a huge range; electric shock (a≈3.5) expands it. Slide the exponent to see the curve bend.

bio_vision_photoreception.caption: Three cone types absorb different wavelengths, and the brain compares their outputs to see colour; rods peak near 498 nm. Slide the wavelength and read each cone's response.

bio_hearing_chemosense.caption: The cochlea is a frequency map (Greenwood function): high pitches vibrate the base, low pitches the apex. Slide along the basilar membrane to read the frequency at each point.

bio_brain_organization.caption: The central nervous system divides into regions with broad roles, from reflex and life-support circuits in the brainstem to planning in the cortex.

bio_autonomic_reflexes.caption: A reflex arc is the shortest loop in the nervous system: stimulus, sensor, spinal cord, motor neuron and muscle, with no brain needed for the fast response.

bio_sleep_circadian.caption: Two-process model: sleep pressure (S, gold) builds while awake and dissipates in sleep, while the body clock (C, blue) rises and falls on a 24 h cycle. Lengthen wakefulness to see pressure climb.

bio_nervous_disorders.caption: In Parkinson's disease, symptoms appear only after most dopamine neurons are lost, since the circuit compensates until a threshold. Slide the threshold to see how late the decline shows.

bio_behavior_proximate_ultimate.caption: Tinbergen's four questions about any behaviour: two ask how it happens (mechanism such as hormones and brain circuits; development such as learning), two ask why it exists (function such as attracting mates; evolutionary history).

bio_learning_social_behavior.caption: Marginal value theorem: a forager should leave a patch when its average rate of gain, counting travel time, is highest. Longer travel between patches means staying longer in each.

bio_migration_navigation.caption: A migrating bird that heads straight at the goal is pushed sideways by wind; it must compensate. Change the wind to see the drift and the resulting ground speed.

bio_neuro_methods.caption: Typical spatial resolution of methods (mm, log scale, approximate): from single-cell recordings to whole-head EEG, there is a trade-off between detail and coverage.

bio_immuno.caption: The immune system has a fast, general innate arm and a slower, specific adaptive arm; they cooperate and the adaptive arm remembers.

bio_innate_immunity.caption: Innate defence in seconds to hours: a macrophage senses microbial patterns, releases cytokines, and calls neutrophils to the site, producing the signs of inflammation.

bio_antigen_presentation_mhc.caption: MHC I shows peptides from inside any cell to killer (CD8) T cells; MHC II shows peptides taken up by antigen-presenting cells to helper (CD4) T cells.

bio_t_cell_immunity.caption: An antigen-presenting cell activates naïve T cells; helper T cells then coordinate other cells while cytotoxic T cells kill infected ones.

bio_b_cells_antibodies.caption: An antibody is Y-shaped: two identical antigen-binding arms (Fab) and a tail (Fc) that signals other immune cells. Move the slider to flex the hinge.

bio_antibody_diversity.caption: V(D)J recombination picks one segment from each gene pool, so a few hundred gene segments give millions of distinct antibodies. Change the pool sizes and watch the total multiply.

bio_immune_memory_clonal.caption: The first exposure gives a slow, low IgM response; a second exposure meets memory cells, so antibody rises faster, higher and lasts longer. Move the slider for the second dose.

bio_vaccines.caption: Herd immunity threshold: when a fraction 1 − 1/R₀ of the population is immune, each case infects fewer than one other person. Diseases with higher R₀ need higher coverage.

bio_hypersensitivity_autoimmunity.caption: Hypersensitivity reactions are grouped by mechanism, from immediate IgE allergy to delayed T-cell reactions; autoimmunity is the same machinery aimed at self.

bio_immunodeficiency_transplant.caption: Host T cells recognise the graft's foreign MHC and attack it; immunosuppressants such as cyclosporine block IL-2 signalling and so T-cell activation.

bio_cancer_immunotherapy.caption: Tumours can switch T cells off by displaying PD-L1 to the PD-1 receptor. Checkpoint-blocking antibodies release the brake so the T cell can kill again.

bio_immunoassays.caption: An ELISA standard curve is S-shaped (4-parameter logistic). Read a sample's absorbance on the curve to find its concentration; the readout inverts the curve.

bio_ecology.caption: Ecology studies life at nested levels: individuals form populations, which form communities, which with their environment make ecosystems and the biosphere.

bio_ecology_scope.caption: Two species use a resource gradient (food size, say). As their niche centres move apart, overlap shrinks and competition weakens. Slide the separation.

bio_population_structure.caption: Survivorship curves: type I (humans) die late, type II (birds) at a constant rate, type III (oysters, fish) die mostly when young. The y-axis is logarithmic.

bio_exponential_logistic_growth.caption: Unlimited growth is exponential (dashed); resources limit it to a logistic S-curve that levels off at the carrying capacity K. Growth is fastest at K/2.

bio_life_history_regulation.caption: Density dependence: birth rate falls and death rate rises as the population grows. They cross at the carrying capacity K, where growth stops. Raise the baseline birth rate to raise K.

bio_metapopulations_human_growth.caption: Levins' model: patches are colonised at rate c and go extinct at rate e. The fraction occupied settles at p* = 1 − e/c, and falls to zero if extinction outpaces colonisation.

bio_competition_predation.caption: Lotka–Volterra predators and prey rise and fall out of step: prey (green) peak first, predators (pink) follow. This small-cycle approximation has period 2π/√(αγ). Change the rates and watch the beat.

bio_symbiosis.caption: Symbiosis covers close, long-term partnerships classed by who gains: both (mutualism), one at no cost to the other (commensalism), or one at the other's expense (parasitism).

bio_community_structure.caption: Shannon diversity H = −Σ pᵢ ln pᵢ with one dominant species at share p and the rest equal. H is highest when all S species are equally common (p = 1/S, H = ln S).
bio_community_structure.xlabel: share of the dominant species p

bio_succession_disturbance.caption: Intermediate disturbance hypothesis: richness peaks at moderate disturbance, where neither dominants nor pioneers take over. Shift the peak to match a different habitat.

bio_food_webs_energy_flow.caption: Energy passed up a food chain falls by about 90% at each step (the 10% rule). Slide the transfer efficiency to see how quickly top predators run out of energy.

bio_primary_production_decomposition.caption: Litter decays exponentially, M = M₀e^(−kt): fast in warm, wet tropics and slow in cold bogs. Slide k to compare habitats.

bio_biogeochemical_cycles_concept.caption: Elements cycle between reservoirs: atmosphere, living things, soil and sediment, and water. Most cycles are closed loops powered by life, light and geology.

bio_biomes.caption: Climate sets biomes: temperature and rainfall place each major biome on this map (approximate annual averages).

bio_biogeography_island.caption: The species–area relationship S = c·Aᶻ: each tenfold increase in island area multiplies species by 10ᶻ. On log axes it is a straight line; the slope z is typically 0.15–0.35.

bio_climate_change_biology.caption: Warming rises with the logarithm of CO₂: each doubling adds the same warming (the climate sensitivity). The dot marks about 420 ppm, relative to a pre-industrial 280 ppm.

bio_biodiversity_crisis.caption: Species–area scaling predicts that losing habitat loses species, but less than proportionally at first: S/S₀ = (A/A₀)ᶻ. Slide z to see how sensitive the species are.

bio_conservation_strategies.caption: With an Allee effect, a population below a threshold A declines to extinction even though it would grow if larger. Raise A and more populations are in danger.

bio_ecosystem_services.caption: Nature supplies four kinds of service that societies depend on, from food and water to climate regulation, recreation and soil formation.

bio_biostats.caption: A typical analysis moves from describing the data to making inferences about the population and then to models that explain it.

bio_descriptive_statistics.caption: About 68% of values lie within one SD of the mean. The standard error s/√n measures how precisely a sample of n estimates that mean; it shrinks as n grows.

bio_distributions_biology.caption: The binomial counts successes in n yes/no trials, such as mutant offspring out of n. It becomes bell-shaped as n grows.

bio_sampling_clt.caption: Even though individual values are skewed (exponential, dashed), the mean of n of them is nearly normal (blue) and gets narrower as n grows. Slide n.

bio_confidence_intervals.caption: Each bar is the confidence interval from one simulated sample. A 95% interval (z = 1.96) misses the true mean in about 1 of 20 samples (red). Widen it and fewer miss.

bio_hypothesis_testing.caption: If the null hypothesis is true, the p-value is the chance of a result at least this extreme: the shaded tail (double it for a two-sided test). Larger z means smaller p.

bio_t_tests.caption: With few samples the t distribution has fatter tails than the normal, so the cutoff for significance is larger. Raise the degrees of freedom and it converges to the normal.

bio_chi_square_tests.caption: The chi-square distribution describes how far observed counts stray from expectation by chance. The shaded area beyond your χ² is the p-value.

bio_anova.caption: ANOVA compares the spread between group means to the spread within groups. Pull the groups apart or tighten them and F rises; overlapping groups give F near 1.

bio_regression_correlation.caption: Least-squares regression picks the line that minimises the squared vertical distances to the points. Move a and b to lower the error; the minimum is near a = 2.2, b = 0.83.

bio_multiple_testing_pvalues.caption: Test many hypotheses and false positives pile up: the chance of at least one is 1 − (1 − α)^m. Bonferroni fixes it by testing each at α/m.

bio_experimental_design_stats.caption: Power is the chance of detecting a real effect. It rises with sample size and effect size d. Slide d to see how many animals per group reach 80% power.

bio_bayesian_inference_bio.caption: Bayes' theorem: even a good test gives many false positives when the condition is rare. The chance a positive is real depends heavily on prevalence.

bio_ode_models_biology.caption: First-order decay, dC/dt = −kC, has the solution C = C₀e^(−kt). Each half-life t½ = ln2/k halves the amount. Slide k.

bio_matrix_population_models.caption: A two-stage Leslie matrix: juveniles survive with probability s, adults have fecundity f. The population grows as λᵗ, where λ is the dominant eigenvalue. Is λ above 1?

bio_bioinformatics_data_analysis.caption: A reproducible workflow keeps raw data untouched, scripts under version control, and every figure regenerable from code.

bio_lab.caption: Laboratory biology combines hands-on techniques, safe working habits, careful records and honest reporting.

bio_lab_safety_biosafety.caption: Biosafety levels rise with the risk of the agent: BSL-1 for harmless strains such as lab E. coli K-12, up to BSL-4 for deadly agents with no treatment, such as Ebola.

bio_light_microscopy.caption: The Abbe limit: the smallest resolvable distance is d = λ/(2·NA). A higher numerical aperture or shorter wavelength resolves finer detail; light microscopes stop near 200 nm.

bio_fluorescence_microscopy.caption: A fluorophore absorbs at one wavelength and emits at a longer one (the Stokes shift), which lets filters separate the faint emission from the bright excitation. GFP: excitation 488, emission 509 nm.

bio_electron_microscopy.caption: Electrons have a far shorter wavelength than light: λ = h/√(2mₑeV(1+eV/2mₑc²)). At 200 kV it is about 2.5 pm, so resolution is limited by lenses, not wavelength.

bio_pipetting_solutions.caption: Dilution rule C₁V₁ = C₂V₂: the volume of stock needed is V₁ = C₂V₂/C₁. A more concentrated stock needs less volume; the rest is made up with buffer.

bio_spectrophotometry.caption: Beer–Lambert law: absorbance A = ε·l·c rises in proportion to concentration. Above A ≈ 2 almost no light gets through and the readings become unreliable. Slide the concentration.

bio_centrifugation_separation.caption: Relative centrifugal force grows with the square of speed: RCF = 1.118×10⁻⁵ · r · rpm². Double the rpm and you quadruple the force. Slide the rotor radius and speed.

bio_cell_culture_aseptic.caption: Cultured cells double every td hours until the dish is confluent, then growth stops, so cultures need splitting. Slow cells reach confluence later.

bio_gfp_reporters.caption: After a reporter gene is switched on, the protein must fold and form its chromophore before it glows, so fluorescence lags. Slow-maturing proteins respond later; slide the maturation half-time.

bio_lab_notebook_reports.caption: Good records let someone repeat your work: plan it, do it, write down exactly what happened, analyse, and report, then refine the plan.

bio_literature_scientific_writing.caption: A research paper follows the IMRaD structure: Introduction (why), Methods (how), Results (what), Discussion (so what).

bio_research_ethics.caption: Research ethics rests on respect for persons, benefit over harm and fairness, plus honest reporting and the 3Rs for animals: replace, reduce, refine.

bio_field_methods.caption: Sample a small square (quadrat) and scale up. Move it around: counts vary between spots, which is why several random quadrats are needed. The true density is 70 plants per 1500 m².

bio_electives.caption: Elective topics apply the core ideas to specific problems: oceans, cancer, drugs, epidemics, engineered life and life elsewhere.

bio_marine_biology.caption: Light fades with depth as I = I₀e^(−kz). Photosynthesis needs more than 1% of surface light, so the sunlit zone is only about 4.6/k deep: ≈ 115 m in clear ocean, ≈ 20 m in murky coastal water.

bio_cancer_hallmarks.caption: Tumour growth follows a Gompertz curve: exponential at first, then slowing as nutrients and space limit it. Compare it with unchecked exponential growth (dashed).

bio_pharmacology_adme.caption: After an IV dose, concentration decays exponentially: C = (Dose/Vd)·e^(−kt) with k = CL/Vd, half-life t½ = 0.693·Vd/CL. Higher clearance or smaller volume shortens it.

bio_toxicology.caption: The dose makes the poison: response rises as an S-curve against log dose. LD₅₀ is the dose that kills half the animals; a steeper curve means a narrower safety margin.

bio_epidemiology.caption: Compare disease risk in exposed and unexposed groups. The risk ratio is the ratio of the bars; the odds ratio (a·d)/(b·c) is similar to it when disease is rare and drifts higher when it is common.

bio_epidemic_modeling.caption: In the SIR model the infected fraction i depends on the susceptible fraction s as i = 1 − s + ln(s)/R₀ (starting from nearly everyone susceptible). Epidemics peak where s = 1/R₀. Raise β to raise R₀ = β/γ.

bio_advanced_endocrinology.caption: Thyroid feedback: pituitary TSH rises exponentially as free T4 falls, so a small drop in T4 gives a large TSH change. Shift the set-point to model a disorder.

bio_virology_advanced.caption: The chance a genome copy is error-free is e^(−μL). RNA viruses mutate about 10⁴ times more per site than DNA viruses and sit near their error limit L ≈ 1/μ, which limits genome size.

bio_bioinformatics_advanced.caption: A ROC curve shows the trade-off between catching true positives and raising false alarms as the threshold moves. Better classifiers bow toward the top-left (higher AUC); the diagonal is guessing.

bio_conservation_genomics.caption: Small populations lose genetic diversity by drift: heterozygosity decays as H = H₀(1 − 1/2Nₑ)ᵗ. A small effective size erodes variation quickly and leaves the species less adaptable.

bio_synthetic_biology.caption: A genetic toggle switch: two repressor genes each shut off the other, so the cell settles stably into one state or the other, an engineered memory.

bio_astrobiology.caption: The habitable zone is where liquid water can exist on a planet's surface. It moves outward for brighter stars (distance scales as √L). Slide the star's luminosity.

bio_systems_biology_networks.caption: Regulatory networks contain recurring motifs. In a feed-forward loop, X controls Z both directly and through Y, which filters out brief noisy signals.

bio_biophysics_elective.caption: Thermal energy kBT ≈ 4.1 pN·nm at 25 °C sets the scale of molecular life. The Boltzmann factor e^(−ε/kBT) gives the odds of a state costing energy ε; an ATP hydrolysis (≈ 80 pN·nm) is ≈ 20 kBT.

bio_microbial_ecology_elective.caption: Monod kinetics: growth rate μ = μmax·S/(Ks + S) saturates when the nutrient is plentiful. Ks is the nutrient level at half the maximum rate.

bio_bioethics_society.caption: Biotechnology raises questions that biology alone cannot settle; four principles help structure the discussion.

bio_genome_organization.caption: Genome size in megabases (log scale, approximate): size does not track complexity, since much of a large genome is repeats and non-coding DNA.

bio_mitochondrial_genome.caption: Each cell holds many mtDNA copies, mutant and normal (heteroplasmy). Disease appears only once the mutant fraction passes a threshold, often 60–90%. Slide the threshold.

bio_riboswitches_ribozymes.caption: A riboswitch is an RNA that binds a small molecule and changes shape, switching its own gene off. Expression falls as ligand rises, with half-point at Kd.

bio_translation_steps.caption: Translation: the ribosome assembles on the start codon, then repeatedly adds amino acids (about 15–20 per second in bacteria) until a stop codon recruits release factors.

bio_chromatin_remodeling_histone_code.caption: Writers add histone marks, erasers remove them, and readers bind marks to open or close chromatin. Acetylation generally opens it; H3K9me3 closes it.

bio_genetic_counseling_screening.caption: For a recessive disease with incidence 1 in n, carrier frequency is 2q(1−q) with q = 1/√n; carriers are far more common than patients. Slide the incidence.

bio_twin_family_studies.caption: Falconer's formula: heritability h² ≈ 2(r_MZ − r_DZ). Identical twins share all genes, fraternal twins half; the bigger the gap between their correlations, the more genetic the trait.

bio_genetic_screens.caption: Forward genetics starts from a phenotype and finds the gene; reverse genetics starts from a gene and finds its phenotype.

bio_roots_mycorrhiza.caption: Nutrient uptake saturates like an enzyme: I = Imax·C/(Km + C). Mycorrhizal fungi extend the absorbing surface, raising Imax, which helps most where soil phosphate is scarce.

bio_plant_secondary_metabolites.caption: Known plant secondary metabolites by class (thousands, approximate): terpenoids are the largest group; caffeine and nicotine are alkaloids, menthol a terpenoid.

bio_plant_stress_drought.caption: As soil dries, abscisic acid closes the stomata: conductance drops sharply near a threshold water potential, saving water but limiting CO₂. Shift the threshold for a drought-tolerant plant.

bio_crop_domestication.caption: Domestication changed yield traits (approximate): wild teosinte carries about 10 kernels per ear, modern maize hundreds; wild tomato fruit weigh a gram or so, cultivated ones hundreds.

bio_plant_pathogens_defense.caption: Plants have two layers: PAMP-triggered immunity catches common microbial patterns, and effector-triggered immunity, via R proteins, recognises specific effectors and can cause a localised hypersensitive cell death.

bio_plant_polyploidy.caption: Bread wheat arose by two hybridisations with genome doubling: AA × BB gave tetraploid emmer (28 chromosomes), and emmer × DD gave hexaploid bread wheat (42).

bio_arachnids_crustaceans.caption: Chelicerates (spiders, scorpions, mites) have eight legs and no antennae; crustaceans have two pairs of antennae and branched limbs.

bio_parasites_helminths.caption: Most hosts carry few worms while a few carry many (aggregation). Lower k makes the distribution more skewed, so treating the heavily infected few has an outsized effect.

bio_evolution_of_flight.caption: Lift balances weight: the minimum flight speed is v = √(2W/(ρ·S·C_L)). Larger animals have higher wing loading and must fly faster, which limits flying animals to about 15 kg.

bio_lichens_fungal_biotech.caption: In a lichen the fungus gives protection, water and minerals; the alga or cyanobacterium returns sugars from photosynthesis.

bio_deuterostome_protostome.caption: In protostomes the first opening of the embryo (blastopore) becomes the mouth; in deuterostomes it becomes the anus and the mouth forms second.

bio_countercurrent_exchange.caption: Water (blue) loses O₂ as it flows 0→1; blood in counter-current flows 1→0 and so is always a little lower than the water beside it (red), leaving at ≈ 90%. In concurrent flow (dashed) blood levels off near 50%.

bio_acid_base_physiology.caption: Henderson–Hasselbalch: pH = 6.1 + log₁₀[HCO₃⁻]/(0.03·PCO₂). Breathing out less CO₂ (high PCO₂) lowers pH; kidneys adjust bicarbonate. Normal: 40 mmHg, 24 mM, pH 7.40.

bio_blood_pressure_control.caption: Mean arterial pressure = cardiac output × resistance, with CO = HR × SV. Raise heart rate or stroke volume, or constrict vessels (higher resistance), and pressure goes up.

bio_exercise_physiology.caption: Energy systems hand over: stored phosphagens power the first seconds, glycolysis the next minute or two, and aerobic metabolism takes over for longer efforts. Shares are approximate.

bio_torpor_hibernation.caption: Metabolic rate falls about Q10-fold for each 10 °C drop in body temperature; torpor adds active suppression on top. At 5 °C a hibernator runs at a few percent of its normal rate.

bio_cytokines_chemokines.caption: Cells follow a chemokine gradient toward its source. Concentration falls as e^(−x/λ) with distance; a larger diffusion length λ gives a longer-range signal. The dot is a neutrophil migrating up the gradient.

bio_hematopoiesis.caption: All blood cells descend from haematopoietic stem cells in bone marrow, which split into myeloid and lymphoid lineages.

bio_complement_system.caption: Three pathways converge on C3 cleavage; the products tag microbes (opsonisation), attract phagocytes (C5a) and assemble the membrane attack complex.

bio_spemann_induction.caption: The organiser secretes BMP inhibitors, so BMP activity is lowest next to it and rises away from it. Tissues read thresholds: low BMP → neural, middle → mesoderm, high → epidermis. Raise the inhibitor strength to push the boundaries outward.

bio_sex_determination_development.caption: A single Y-linked gene, SRY, switches the gonad toward testis; without it the gonad becomes an ovary, and the hormones each gonad makes direct the rest of development.

bio_axis_symmetry_breaking.caption: Bicoid mRNA is localised at the embryo's front and its protein forms a gradient, c = e^(−x/λ). Hunchback turns on where Bicoid exceeds a threshold, so doubling the Bicoid dose moves the boundary toward the back by λ·ln2.

bio_flow_cytometry.caption: Each cell is a point in scatter space; clusters are cell types (lymphocytes small and smooth, monocytes mid, granulocytes large and granular). Draw a gate to count or sort one population.

bio_calibration_standard_curves.caption: A standard curve converts signal to concentration. The limit of detection LOD ≈ 3.3σ/slope falls as the noise σ falls. Increase the blank noise to see detection get worse.

bio_western_blot_elisa_protocols.caption: A Western blot: separate proteins by size, transfer them to a membrane, block, probe with antibodies, and image the bands.

bio_ecosystem_stability.caption: Net growth of a lake or rangeland under grazing or nutrient load c: dx/dt = rx(1 − x/K) − c·x²/(1 + x²). Raise c and the stable states vanish at a tipping point; the system jumps to a degraded state.

bio_pollination_networks.caption: Plants (green) and pollinators (gold) form a nested web: specialists (P3, P4; A4, A5) tie to generalists (P1, A1). Watch the links light up; losing a generalist hurts many partners.

bio_soil_ecology.caption: The soil food web: plant litter feeds bacteria and fungi, which are eaten by protozoa and nematodes, which in turn feed mites and larger predators, releasing nutrients to plants.

bio_processes.caption: Life runs on a handful of step-by-step processes, from copying and reading genes to extracting energy, building sugar, dividing, and passing signals.

dna_replication_process.caption: DNA replication follows six steps: the helicase opens the origin, primase starts each strand, and the lagging strand is made in Okazaki fragments joined by ligase.

transcription_process.caption: RNA polymerase binds the promoter, opens the DNA, elongates the RNA, and stops; in eukaryotes the transcript is then capped, tailed, spliced and exported.

glycolysis_process.caption: Glycolysis invests 2 ATP, splits a six-carbon sugar into two three-carbon pieces and recovers 4 ATP, a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose.

krebs_cycle_process.caption: The citric acid cycle is a loop: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate, two carbons leave as CO₂, and oxaloacetate is regenerated, yielding 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 ATP per turn.

oxidative_phosphorylation_process.caption: NADH and FADH₂ give electrons to the chain, which pumps protons to build a gradient; protons flowing back through ATP synthase make ≈ 2.5 ATP per NADH.

photosynthesis_light_process.caption: Light excites photosystems, splitting water and releasing O₂; the electron flow pumps protons for ATP and finally reduces NADP⁺ to NADPH.

calvin_cycle_process.caption: Rubisco fixes CO₂ onto RuBP, ATP and NADPH reduce it, one G3P in six leaves as sugar, and the rest regenerates RuBP: 3 turns fix 3 CO₂ for 1 G3P.

meiosis_process.caption: DNA content per cell (C) over meiosis: replication doubles it, meiosis I halves the chromosome number, and meiosis II halves it again to give four haploid gametes.

pcr_process.caption: Each PCR cycle (denature, anneal, extend) ideally doubles the DNA: copies = N₀(1 + E)ⁿ. Lower efficiency E slows the climb; 30 cycles from one molecule gives about a billion.

crispr_editing_process.caption: A guide RNA leads Cas9 to a matching DNA site next to a PAM; Cas9 cuts both strands and the cell repairs the break, either imprecisely (knockout) or from a template (edit).

viral_replication_process.caption: One-step growth curve: after attachment and entry the virus seems to disappear (the eclipse), then a burst releases new particles. Slide the latent period and burst size.

natural_selection_process.caption: Variation, differential survival and inheritance shift allele frequency: p(t) = p₀(1+s)ᵗ / (1 − p₀ + p₀(1+s)ᵗ). A bigger advantage s means faster change.

speciation_process.caption: After populations are separated, they drift and adapt to different conditions; their trait distributions pull apart and the overlap, where hybrids would form, shrinks. Slide the time apart.

nitrogen_cycle_process.caption: Nitrogen gas is fixed by bacteria into ammonium, nitrified to nitrate, taken up by plants, returned by decay (ammonification) and finally denitrified back to N₂.

carbon_cycle_process.caption: Arrows: photosynthesis and respiration, litter and decay, dissolving and outgassing. Carbon moves between air (≈ 880 GtC), plants (≈ 550), soil (≈ 1,500+), oceans (≈ 38,000 mostly deep) and rock. Burning fossil fuels moves stored carbon into the air faster than sinks absorb it.

signal_transduction_process.caption: A kinase cascade amplifies a signal: if each activated enzyme activates m copies of the next, n steps give mⁿ activated molecules from a single receptor event.

vaccine_immunity_process.caption: A vaccine shows the immune system a harmless antigen: it is taken up, presented, activates T and B cells, and leaves long-lived memory cells without causing disease.

gastrulation_process.caption: In gastrulation a two-layer disc is reorganised into three germ layers: cells ingress through the primitive streak to form endoderm and mesoderm, leaving ectoderm on top.

sanger_ngs_sequencing_process.caption: Sanger reads one fragment at a time by chain termination; next-generation sequencing reads millions of clusters in parallel and assembles them by computer.
